title: Toggle Tailwind v4 dark: with a button
summary: In v4, dark: follows the OS setting by default, so adding a dark class changes nothing. Tie it to .dark with @custom-variant, remember the choice, and stop the flash on load with a script in head.

files.content:
Dashboard

No reports yet.

turns.user: dark mode button does nothing. switching the OS to dark does. and i have darkMode: class in tailwind.config.js

assistant.body: Sure. In Tailwind v4, dark: is a prefers-color-scheme media query by default, so it only listens to the OS. darkMode: 'class' is the v3 setting in tailwind.config.js. v4 is configured in CSS and does not read that file unless you load it with @config. Instead, declare a @custom-variant in the CSS that ties dark: to the .dark class. It matches the element carrying .dark and everything inside it.
The class goes on html rather than body. Later on the theme will be decided from head, where body does not exist yet.

turns.user: works! but a reload resets it. save it. and first visit should follow the OS

assistant.body: Perfect, two small pieces. A click saves the choice to localStorage. On load the saved value wins, and without one matchMedia asks the OS. classList.toggle takes a second argument that forces the class on or off, so the result can go straight in. localStorage is now the single source of truth for the theme.

<script>
      const root = document.documentElement
      const saved = localStorage.getItem('theme')
      const prefersDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches
      root.classList.toggle('dark', saved ? saved === 'dark' : prefersDark)

      document.querySelector('#theme-toggle').addEventListener('click', () => {
        const dark = root.classList.toggle('dark')
        localStorage.setItem('theme', dark ? 'dark' : 'light')
      })
    </script>

turns.user: saving works. but reloading in dark flashes white for a moment

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer missed this. The setup sat at the end of body, so the browser can paint the light page once before it gets there. The theme has to be decided before the first paint, inside head. The three setup lines at the bottom go first. Note: the same const in two scripts makes the second one fail with a SyntaxError, and the button would stop working with it.
In head it has to be a plain script, with neither defer nor type="module". Both of those postpone it, and the flash comes back.

<head>
    <meta charset="utf-8">
    <title>Dashboard</title>
    <script>
      const saved = localStorage.getItem('theme')
      const prefersDark = matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches
      document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', saved ? saved === 'dark' : prefersDark)
    </script>
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="/dist/app.css">
  </head>
